alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of an old printed title page inside a wide border of repeating interlaced leaf ornament. It reads "Deuteromelia: or The Second part of Musicks melodie, or melodius Musicke. Of Pleasant Roundelaies; K. H. mirth, or Freemens Songs. And such delightfull Catches. Qui canere potest canat. Catch, that catch can. Vt Mel Os, sic Cor melos afficit, & reficit. London: Printed for Thomas Adams, dwelling in Paules Church-yard at the signe of the white Lion. 1609."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de una antigua portada impresa dentro de un ancho marco de adorno de hojas entrelazadas que se repite. Dice "Deuteromelia: or The Second part of Musicks melodie, or melodius Musicke. Of Pleasant Roundelaies; K. H. mirth, or Freemens Songs. And such delightfull Catches. Qui canere potest canat. Catch, that catch can. Vt Mel Os, sic Cor melos afficit, & reficit. London: Printed for Thomas Adams, dwelling in Paules Church-yard at the signe of the white Lion. 1609."

caption.en: The title page of Deuteromelia, printed in London for Thomas Adams in 1609: the book of rounds and catches that holds the earliest known printing of Three Blind Mice, as No. 13.
caption.es: La portada de Deuteromelia, impresa en Londres para Thomas Adams en 1609: el libro de cánones y catches que contiene la primera impresión conocida de Three Blind Mice, el n.º 13.

source: [Thomas Ravenscroft, compiler], Deuteromelia: or The Second part of Musicks melodie (London: printed [by T. Snodham] for Thomas Adams, 1609; STC 20757), title page (image n0); cropped to the bordered page, leaving out a later handwritten name and number above it
library: Internet Archive, Early English Books 1475-1640 microfilm (holding library not named on the film)
licenceEvidence: Printed 1609, anonymous (preface signed "T. R."); credited compiler Thomas Ravenscroft died about 1630 to 1635 (no later than about 1640), printer Thomas Snodham died 1624, bookseller Thomas Adams died 1620. Microfilm scan with no holder named; IA metadata has no rights field; PD-old by age. See rights.md.
credit: Internet Archive, Early English Books microfilm

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of two staves of early printed music with diamond-shaped notes, the second ending after three notes and a rest, the rest of the staff left empty. The words under them read "Iulian, the Miller and his merry olde Wife, shee scrapte her tripe licke thou the knife."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de dos pentagramas de música impresa antigua con notas en forma de rombo; el segundo termina tras tres notas y un silencio, y el resto del pentagrama queda vacío. La letra debajo dice "Iulian, the Miller and his merry olde Wife, shee scrapte her tripe licke thou the knife."

caption.en: The second and third staves of No. 13, "Three blinde Mice", in Deuteromelia (London, 1609): in the earliest known words there is no farmer's wife, only "the Miller and his merry olde Wife" and her tripe.
caption.es: El segundo y el tercer pentagrama del n.º 13, "Three blinde Mice", en Deuteromelia (Londres, 1609): en la letra más antigua conocida no hay mujer del granjero, solo "the Miller and his merry olde Wife" (el molinero y su alegre y vieja mujer) y sus callos.

source: [Thomas Ravenscroft, compiler], Deuteromelia (London: printed [by T. Snodham] for Thomas Adams, 1609; STC 20757), p. 12, No. 13, "Three blinde Mice", Rounds or Catches of 3. Voices (image n21); cropped to the round's second and third staves
library: Internet Archive, Early English Books 1475-1640 microfilm (holding library not named on the film)
licenceEvidence: Printed 1609, anonymous; credited compiler Thomas Ravenscroft died about 1630 to 1635, printer Thomas Snodham died 1624, bookseller Thomas Adams died 1620. Microfilm scan with no holder named; IA metadata has no rights field; PD-old by age. See rights.md.
credit: Internet Archive, Early English Books microfilm

alt.en: Printed text on a white page, headed "LXX.", in three lines: "Three blind mice, the three blind mice, They all ran after the farmer's wife, Who cut off their tails with the carving-knife."
alt.es: Texto impreso en una página blanca, con el encabezado "LXX.", en tres versos: "Three blind mice, the three blind mice, They all ran after the farmer's wife, Who cut off their tails with the carving-knife."

caption.en: No. LXX in James Orchard Halliwell's The Nursery Rhymes of England (London, 1842): the earliest printing of the farmer's wife and her carving-knife that we found.
caption.es: El n.º LXX de The Nursery Rhymes of England, de James Orchard Halliwell (Londres, 1842): la impresión más antigua de la mujer del granjero y su cuchillo de trinchar que hemos encontrado.

source: James Orchard Halliwell, ed., The Nursery Rhymes of England (London: printed for the Percy Society by T. Richards, 1842), in Early English Poetry, Ballads, and Popular Literature of the Middle Ages, vol. 4, p. 43, No. LXX (image n313); cropped to No. LXX
callNumber: Digital Library of India 2015.89222; Internet Archive in.ernet.dli.2015.89222, image n313
licenceEvidence: Title page dated MDCCCXLII (1842); words traditional; editor James Orchard Halliwell (later Halliwell-Phillipps) died 1889; printed by T. Richards, a London printer active in 1842. Faithful scan of a flat page; IA metadata has no rights field; PD-old by age. See rights.md.
credit: Digital Library of India, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A yellowed music page headed "Three Blind Mice" and "(Round in Four Parts)": three lines of melody in 6/8 with two sharps, numbered 1 and 2 on the first line, 3 on the second and 4 on the third. The words read "Three blind mice, Three blind mice, See how they run! See how they run! They all ran after the farmer's wife; She cut off their tails with a carving knife: Did ever you see such a sight in your life, As three blind mice."
alt.es: Una página de música amarillenta con el encabezado "Three Blind Mice" y "(Round in Four Parts)": tres líneas de melodía en 6/8 con dos sostenidos, numeradas 1 y 2 en la primera línea, 3 en la segunda y 4 en la tercera. La letra dice "Three blind mice, Three blind mice, See how they run! See how they run! They all ran after the farmer's wife; She cut off their tails with a carving knife: Did ever you see such a sight in your life, As three blind mice."

caption.en: "Three Blind Mice (Round in Four Parts)" on page 95 of Home Songs (Boston: Oliver Ditson Company, 1906), the page our round is sung from, a whole tone lower; the numbers mark where each voice comes in.
caption.es: "Three Blind Mice (Round in Four Parts)" en la página 95 de Home Songs (Boston: Oliver Ditson Company, 1906), la página de la que cantamos nuestro canon, un tono más abajo; los números marcan dónde entra cada voz.

source: Home Songs: A Collection of Favorite Songs, Hymns and Rounds for the Fireside (Boston: Oliver Ditson Company, 1906), p. 95, "Three Blind Mice (Round in Four Parts)" (image n100); cropped to the round, leaving out the song above it
library: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: University of Illinois 784.3 H752; Internet Archive homesongscollect00unse_0, image n100
licenceEvidence: Published Boston 1906 (title page: "Copyright, mcmvi, by Oliver Ditson Company"), before 1931, so public domain in the US; the title page names no editor or arranger, and the round's words and tune are traditional, printed with no name; a company's anonymous work of 1906 is past 100 years from publication (Mexico) and 70 (EU, Israel). Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.
credit: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, via the Internet Archive
